0: //! A write-once key-value store for ordered data.
1: //!
2: //! [Archive] is a key-value store designed for workloads where data is written only once and each
3: //! item is addressed by both an `index` and a `key`. Workloads with unique indices should use [Archive]
4: //! and workloads with overlapping indices should use [MultiArchive] (allows all items with the same index
5: //! to be retrieved). The same key may be stored at multiple indices in either case, and a key lookup may
6: //! return any of the associated values.
7: 
8: use commonware_codec::Codec;
9: use commonware_runtime::Handle;
10: use commonware_utils::Array;
11: use std::future::Future;
12: use thiserror::Error;
13: 
14: pub mod immutable;
15: pub mod prunable;
16: 
17: #[cfg(all(test, feature = "arbitrary"))]
18: mod conformance;
19: 
20: /// Subject of a `get` or `has` operation.
21: pub enum Identifier<'a, K: Array> {
22:     Index(u64),
23:     Key(&'a K),
24: }
25: 
26: /// Errors that can occur when interacting with the archive.
27: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
28: pub enum Error {
29:     #[error("journal error: {0}")]
30:     Journal(crate::journal::Error),
31:     #[error("ordinal error: {0}")]
32:     Ordinal(#[from] crate::ordinal::Error),
33:     #[error("metadata error: {0}")]
34:     Metadata(#[from] crate::metadata::Error),
35:     #[error("freezer error: {0}")]
36:     Freezer(#[from] crate::freezer::Error),
37:     #[error("record corrupted")]
38:     RecordCorrupted,
39: }
40: 
41: // Preserve the archive's error classification for journal-owned metadata operations.
42: impl From<crate::journal::Error> for Error {
43:     fn from(error: crate::journal::Error) -> Self {
44:         match error {
45:             crate::journal::Error::Metadata(error) => Self::Metadata(error),
46:             error => Self::Journal(error),
47:         }
48:     }
49: }

51: /// A write-once key-value store addressed by both an index and a key.
52: ///
53: /// Mutating functions consume the archive and return it only on success: an error (or a
54: /// dropped future) destroys the handle. Pruning implementations satisfy puts below the prune
55: /// floor without storing: pruning declared that range obsolete, so nothing is mutated and
56: /// nothing below the floor is ever readable.
57: pub trait Archive: Send + Sized {
58:     /// The type of the key.
59:     type Key: Array;
60: 
61:     /// The type of the value.
62:     type Value: Codec + Send;
63: 
64:     /// Store an item in [Archive].
65:     ///
66:     /// Indices are unique: if the index already exists, put does nothing and returns. Duplicate
67:     /// indices can be stored via [MultiArchive::put_multi]. Keys need not be unique: the same key
68:     /// may be stored at multiple indices, and a subsequent [Archive::get] or [Archive::has] call
69:     /// with an [Identifier::Key] identifier may return any of the values associated with that key.
70:     ///
71:     /// A put below the prune floor is satisfied without storing (see the trait docs).
72:     fn put(
73:         self,
74:         index: u64,
75:         key: Self::Key,
76:         value: Self::Value,
77:     ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Self, Error>> + Send;
78: 
79:     /// Perform a [Archive::put] and [Archive::sync] in a single operation.
80:     fn put_sync(
81:         self,
82:         index: u64,
83:         key: Self::Key,
84:         value: Self::Value,
85:     ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Self, Error>> + Send {
86:         async move { self.put(index, key, value).await?.sync().await }
87:     }
88: 
89:     /// Perform a [Archive::put] and [Archive::start_sync] in a single operation.
90:     ///
91:     /// If the index already exists (making the put a no-op), the returned handle still reports
92:     /// the durability of all previously accepted writes, including the original write for this
93:     /// index if its sync is still in flight.
94:     fn put_start_sync(
95:         self,
96:         index: u64,
97:         key: Self::Key,
98:         value: Self::Value,
99:     ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(Self, Handle<()>), Error>> + Send {
100:         async move { self.put(index, key, value).await?.start_sync().await }
101:     }
102: 
103:     /// Retrieve an item from [Archive].
104:     ///
105:     /// Note that if the [Archive] is a [MultiArchive], there may be multiple values associated with the
106:     /// same [Identifier::Index]. If there are multiple values, the first stored will be returned. Use
107:     /// [MultiArchive::get_all] to retrieve all values at an index.
108:     fn get<'a>(
109:         &'a self,
110:         identifier: Identifier<'a, Self::Key>,
111:     ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Option<Self::Value>, Error>> + Send + use<'a, Self>;
112: 
113:     /// Check if an item exists in [Archive].
114:     fn has<'a>(
115:         &'a self,
116:         identifier: Identifier<'a, Self::Key>,
117:     ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, Error>> + Send + use<'a, Self>;
118: 
119:     /// Retrieve the end of the current range including `index` (inclusive) and
120:     /// the start of the next range after `index` (if it exists).
121:     ///
122:     /// This is useful for driving backfill operations over the archive.
123:     fn next_gap(&self, index: u64) -> (Option<u64>, Option<u64>);
124: 
125:     /// Returns up to `max` missing items starting from `start`.
126:     ///
127:     /// This method iterates through gaps between existing ranges, collecting missing indices
128:     /// until either `max` items are found or there are no more gaps to fill.
129:     fn missing_items(&self, index: u64, max: usize) -> Vec<u64>;
130: 
131:     /// Retrieve an iterator over all populated ranges (inclusive) within the [Archive].
132:     fn ranges(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (u64, u64)>;
133: 
134:     /// Retrieve an iterator over ranges that overlap or follow `from`.
135:     fn ranges_from(&self, from: u64) -> impl Iterator<Item = (u64, u64)>;
136: 
137:     /// Retrieve the first index in the [Archive].
138:     fn first_index(&self) -> Option<u64>;
139: 
140:     /// Retrieve the last index in the [Archive].
141:     fn last_index(&self) -> Option<u64>;
142: 
143:     /// Sync all pending writes.
144:     fn sync(self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Self, Error>> + Send;
145: 
146:     /// Request that all pending writes are synced.
147:     ///
148:     /// The returned handle completes once every write accepted before this call is durable,
149:     /// including writes covered by a sync that is still in flight. Implementations without a
150:     /// non-blocking sync path may complete the sync before returning an already-finished handle.
151:     ///
152:     /// An error reported by the returned [Handle] is fatal to the archive: the caller must
153:     /// stop using the returned archive.
154:     fn start_sync(self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(Self, Handle<()>), Error>> + Send {
155:         async move {
156:             let archive = self.sync().await?;
157:             Ok((archive, Handle::ready(Ok(()))))
158:         }
159:     }
160: 
161:     /// Remove all persistent data created by this [Archive].
162:     fn destroy(self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Error>> + Send;
163: }
164: 
165: /// Extension of [Archive] that supports multiple items at the same index.
166: ///
167: /// Unlike [Archive::put], which is a no-op when the index already exists,
168: /// [MultiArchive::put_multi] allows storing additional `(key, value)` pairs
169: /// at an existing index.
170: pub trait MultiArchive: Archive {
171:     /// Retrieve all values stored at the given index.
172:     ///
173:     /// Returns `None` if the index does not exist or has been pruned.
174:     fn get_all(
175:         &self,
176:         index: u64,
177:     ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Option<Vec<Self::Value>>, Error>> + Send + use<'_, Self>;
178: 
179:     /// Check whether `key` is stored at `index`.
180:     ///
181:     /// Unlike [Archive::has] with [Identifier::Key], the check is scoped to a
182:     /// single index. Unlike [MultiArchive::get_all], no values are fetched.
183:     fn has_at<'a>(
184:         &'a self,
185:         index: u64,
186:         key: &'a Self::Key,
187:     ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, Error>> + Send + use<'a, Self>;
188: 
189:     /// Store an item, allowing multiple items at the same index.
190:     ///
191:     /// Multiple items may share the same `index`. If the same key is stored at
192:     /// multiple indices, any associated value may be returned when queried with
193:     /// [Identifier::Key].
194:     ///
195:     /// A put below the prune floor is satisfied without storing (see the trait docs).
196:     fn put_multi(
197:         self,
198:         index: u64,
199:         key: Self::Key,
200:         value: Self::Value,
201:     ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Self, Error>> + Send;
202: 
203:     /// Perform a [MultiArchive::put_multi] and [Archive::sync] in a single operation.
204:     fn put_multi_sync(
205:         self,
206:         index: u64,
207:         key: Self::Key,
208:         value: Self::Value,
209:     ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Self, Error>> + Send {
210:         async move { self.put_multi(index, key, value).await?.sync().await }
211:     }
212: 
213:     /// Perform a [MultiArchive::put_multi] and [Archive::start_sync] in a single operation.
214:     fn put_multi_start_sync(
215:         self,
216:         index: u64,
217:         key: Self::Key,
218:         value: Self::Value,
219:     ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(Self, Handle<()>), Error>> + Send {
220:         async move { self.put_multi(index, key, value).await?.start_sync().await }
